hotspots.resolution: Startup/mode/session/model/reload/prompt and command workflows have concrete owners. Active project, model and conversation bindings publish named transitions instead of scattered mutable root locals; root retains bootstrap, implementation selection, resource leases and transparent UI/protocol wiring.

Timed scheduling, conversation presentation/live sources and status/authorization state have concrete owners. Screen retains terminal mode/writer lifetime, shared state locking, viewport/editor/panel state and frame composition; original render/capture/reflow/cleanup order remains explicit.

Per-attempt provider turn journal, physical request usage attribution and stream progress/disposal have distinct owners; run retains explicit prompt/retry/compaction orchestration and canonical settlement ordering under existing locks.

Native message/document conversion and canonical context/usage/compaction projection have distinct owners; session retains tree/metadata mutation and branch state. Internal codec forwarding removed; public APIs and format unchanged.
Import/version migration, entry/content codec, ordered private writer and bounded run projection have distinct owners; internal forwarding facade calls removed while public compatibility APIs remain.

Compaction summarizer request lifecycle and configured tool catalog/session loadouts have concrete owners; PiAgent owns direct MAF execution, active run state and durable executable binding. Public option-rich constructor preserved for compatibility; no options bag or new interfaces.

Provider credential precedence/binding, synchronized available snapshots and serialized router cache/profile discovery have distinct concrete owners; runtime coordinates catalog/scope/model selection in CLI.
Distinct file-reading, file-mutation, shell-execution and Pi declaration owners; public compatibility facade remains direct.
SDK connection/discovery/auth lifetime, tool schema/result publication and shared resource publication have concrete internal owners; runtime selects servers and coordinates startup/live publication.
